archetypes.name: sentinel-touch-conditions
archetypes.rationale: The --preview-only sentinel-touch decision tree has three distinct branches (header-present, empty-plan, allowlist-fail) whose completeness and harness coverage the static panel is unlikely to audit line-by-line.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the plan's multi-branch sentinel-touch logic for `run-step3-review.sh --preview-only`: touch when renderer output contains `## Plan Candidate for Review`, touch when `plan.txt` is missing/empty, and explicitly NOT touch when the allowlist/tmpdir check fails. Determine whether the plan accounts for the case where the renderer exits non-zero but produces non-empty output lacking the header, and whether `LARCH_QUIET_DISABLE` FD-routing changes affect which output stream is inspected for the header. Verify that the `test-run-step3-review.sh` updates cover all three branches and include a case where the renderer produces unexpected non-empty, non-header output. Flag any gaps between the failure-modes section's sentinel-split-ownership and sentinel-over-eager-touch mitigations and the actual touch-condition logic described in the plan. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: thin-fence-kv-ordering
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces a novel KV-precedence rule (later-stdout-wins when no safe env loaded; file-first otherwise) that must be consistently specified across SKILL.md, the harness mock, and the failure-modes section — a cross-file contract consistency check the static panel rarely performs in detail.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine whether the plan's KV-precedence rule — later stdout KVs overwrite earlier fallback values when no safe result env was loaded, while safe result-env values remain authoritative otherwise — is stated consistently across the SKILL.md thin-fence description, the `test-step3-orchestrator-fence.sh` `apply_step3_handoff` update, and the display/KV-bleed failure-modes entry. Verify that the plan specifies which keys constitute the KV allowlist for stdout-fallback parsing, since an underspecified allowlist risks plan-body lines being parsed as terminal state and corrupting the branch matrix. Check whether both the 'safe env loaded → file-first' and 'no safe env → terminal-KV-wins' branches are called out as distinct new test cases in `test-step3-orchestrator-fence.sh`, and whether the later-KV-wins case uses a plan-body line that resembles an allowlisted key to exercise the boundary. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
